title: Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers to 1 000 000
seo_title: Grade 5 Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers Worksheets: Large Numbers and Regrouping (BC)
standard_text: Addition and subtraction of whole numbers to 1 000 000
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on adding and subtracting whole numbers to 1 000 000, matched to the BC curriculum: column addition, subtracting across zeros, estimating first, checking with the inverse and BC word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the ones. Regroup when you need to. Check with the inverse.
key_sub: Estimate before you start. In columns, start on the right; every 0 you regroup across becomes 9. Then add back what you took away to check.
body_html:
The idea: use place value

Numbers to 1 000 000 have hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Add or subtract the same places. When a place gets 10 or more, regroup 10 of them as 1 of the next place.

The method is the same as with smaller numbers. There are just more columns, so line them up carefully.

Column addition

Put ones under ones. Start on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and regroup 1 into the next column.

Line up the ones

What is 352 846 + 41 275?

41 275 has only five digits. Its 5 goes under the 6 in the ones column, not under the 3. 352 846 + 41 275 = 394 121.

Answer: 394 121

Subtraction across zeros

Take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, regroup 1 from the next column. If the next column is 0, go left to the first digit that is not 0. Every 0 you pass becomes 9.

Estimate first, then check with the inverse

Before you start, estimate. Round each number and work it out in your head. For 458 769 + 276 548, 500 000 + 300 000 = 800 000, so the answer should be close to 800 000.

When you finish, check with the inverse. Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check 600 000 − 248 365 = 351 635, add: 351 635 + 248 365 = 600 000. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the numbers on the left (352 846 + 41 275 = 765 596)Line up the ones on the right: 352 846 + 41 275 = 394 121
Not regrouping (458 769 + 276 548 = 624 207)Write the regrouped 1 under the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (503 214 − 186 597 = 483 383)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Regroup when the top is smaller
Making each 0 into 10 instead of 9 (600 000 − 248 365 = 362 745)Only the ones get 10. Each 0 you pass gives 1 away, so it becomes 9

faq.q: What does Grade 5 learn about adding and subtracting in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: Under Computational fluency, Grade 5 students add and subtract whole numbers to 1 000 000. They use the column method with regrouping, estimate first and check their answers with the inverse.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 600 000 − 248 365?
faq.a: Go left to the first digit that is not 0 and regroup from there; each 0 you pass becomes 9. 600 000 becomes 5 hundred thousands, 9 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 600 000 − 248 365 = 351 635.

faq.q: Why should students estimate before adding or subtracting large numbers?
faq.a: An estimate shows about how big the answer should be. If the exact answer is far from the estimate, a column was misaligned or a regrouping was missed.

faq.q: How do you check a subtraction answer with the inverse?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number you took away. For 600 000 − 248 365 = 351 635, 351 635 + 248 365 = 600 000, so the answer is right.

items.e: 452 378 rounds to 450 000 and 36 541 rounds to 40 000. 450 000 + 40 000 = 490 000. 817 788 is far from 490 000, so the answer is not reasonable. The exact answer is 488 919. (Simran lined up 36 541 on the left, not under the ones.)

items.q: Owen worked out 712 406 − 285 739 = 426 667. Estimate to the nearest ten thousand. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: 712 406 rounds to 710 000 and 285 739 rounds to 290 000. 710 000 − 290 000 = 420 000. 426 667 is close to 420 000, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: Chloe worked out 630 000 − 274 568 = 444 568. Estimate to the nearest ten thousand. Is her answer reasonable?

items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 236 688 + 387 462 = 624 150. You get back to the start, so the answer is right.

sets.title: Word problems: BC populations and distances

items.q: In the 2021 census, Kelowna had 144 576 people and Kamloops had 97 902 people. How many people lived in the two cities altogether?
In the 2021 census, Nanaimo had 99 863 people and Prince George had 76 708 people. How many more people lived in Nanaimo?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 99 863 − 76 708 = 23 155. Check: 23 155 + 76 708 = 99 863.

items.q: In the 2021 census, Victoria had 91 867 people and its neighbour Saanich had 117 735 people. How many people lived in the two places altogether?
In the 2021 census, Burnaby had 249 125 people and Richmond had 209 937 people. How many more people lived in Burnaby?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 249 125 − 209 937 = 39 188. Check: 39 188 + 209 937 = 249 125.

items.q: In the 2021 census, Vancouver had 662 248 people and Burnaby had 249 125 people. How many people lived in the two cities altogether?
In the 2021 census, Vancouver had 662 248 people and Surrey had 568 322 people. How many fewer people lived in Surrey?
items.e: How many fewer means find the difference, so subtract. 662 248 − 568 322 = 93 926. Check: 93 926 + 568 322 = 662 248.

items.q: When the Dhillon family bought their van, the odometer showed 48 579 km. Now it shows 213 006 km. How far have they driven the van?
items.e: Find the distance between the two readings, so subtract. 213 006 − 48 579 = 164 427. Check: 164 427 + 48 579 = 213 006.

items.q: Before a road trip from Surrey to Prince George and back, the odometer on the Gill family’s car showed 99 865 km. The trip was 1586 km. What did the odometer show after the trip?
items.e: The car drove more kilometres, so add. 99 865 + 1586 = 101 451. Check: 101 451 − 1586 = 99 865.

items.q: A floatplane company plans to fly 250 000 km this year between Vancouver and Vancouver Island. So far its planes have flown 168 475 km. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Find the distance still to fly, so subtract. 250 000 − 168 475 = 81 525. Check: 81 525 + 168 475 = 250 000.

items.q: One BC ferry sailed 48 675 km in the spring and 52 390 km in the summer. How far did it sail in the two seasons?
items.e: Put the two seasons together, so add. 48 675 + 52 390 = 101 065. Check: 101 065 − 52 390 = 48 675.

items.q: Volunteers counted 486 275 sockeye salmon on the Adams River in one week and 357 948 the next week. How many sockeye did they count in the two weeks?
items.e: Put the two weeks together, so add. 486 275 + 357 948 = 844 223. Check: 844 223 − 357 948 = 486 275.

items.q: Students in a school district set a goal to walk and bike 300 000 km to school this year. So far they have logged 186 475 km. How many more kilometres do they need?
items.e: Find what is still needed, so subtract. 300 000 − 186 475 = 113 525. Check: 113 525 + 186 475 = 300 000.

items.q: A ski hill had some visits before New Year’s Day. After New Year’s Day it had 186 395 more visits. The season total was 452 080 visits. How many visits were there before New Year’s Day?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 186 395 that came later: 452 080 − 186 395 = 265 685. Check: 265 685 + 186 395 = 452 080.

items.q: A SkyTrain station had 248 675 riders in September. In October it had 36 480 more riders than in September. How many riders did it have in the two months?
items.e: Step 1, October’s riders: 248 675 + 36 480 = 285 155. Step 2, both together: 248 675 + 285 155 = 533 830.

items.q: A hockey arena in Kamloops sold 186 425 tickets last season. This season it sold 24 860 fewer. How many tickets did it sell in the two seasons?
items.e: Step 1, this season’s tickets: 186 425 − 24 860 = 161 565. Step 2, both together: 186 425 + 161 565 = 347 990.

items.q: A tree nursery had 450 000 cedar seedlings. It sent 286 475 to be planted in forests. Then it grew 175 650 more. How many seedlings does the nursery have now?
items.e: Step 1, after sending some out: 450 000 − 286 475 = 163 525. Step 2, after growing more: 163 525 + 175 650 = 339 175.

items.q: A library system in the Lower Mainland has 750 000 books. 286 450 books are checked out and 48 675 are being repaired. How many books are on the shelves?
items.e: Step 1, books not on the shelves: 286 450 + 48 675 = 335 125. Step 2, books on the shelves: 750 000 − 335 125 = 414 875.

items.q: In the 2021 census, Vancouver had 662 248 people. Burnaby had 249 125 and Richmond had 209 937. How many more people lived in Vancouver than in Burnaby and Richmond together?
items.e: Step 1, Burnaby and Richmond together: 249 125 + 209 937 = 459 062. Step 2, the difference: 662 248 − 459 062 = 203 186.

items.q: In the 2021 census, Kamloops had 97 902 people and Nanaimo had 99 863. Kelowna had 144 576. How many more people lived in Kamloops and Nanaimo together than in Kelowna?
items.e: Step 1, Kamloops and Nanaimo together: 97 902 + 99 863 = 197 765. Step 2, find the difference: 197 765 − 144 576 = 53 189.

items.q: Leah’s family drove 2486 km on a trip to the Okanagan and 1375 km on a trip around Vancouver Island. Wei’s family drove 5000 km on a summer road trip through Alberta and back. How many more kilometres did Wei’s family drive?
items.e: Step 1, Leah’s family: 2486 + 1375 = 3861. Step 2, find the difference: 5000 − 3861 = 1139.
